question.long: Does video surveillance reduce crime rates?

description: Results from studies evaluating the impact of video surveillance on crime rates in public spaces.

no_consensus.description: The literature has not yet reached a consensus on the effects of video surveillance on crime rates

no.description: The literature suggests that video surveillance does not reduce crime rates

towards_no.description: The literature suggests that video surveillance probably doesn't reduce crime rates, but more research is needed

towards_yes.description: The literature suggests that video surveillance may reduce crime rates, but more research is needed

yes.description: The literature suggests that video surveillance reduces crime rates

no.description: The results of the paper show no significant effect of the video surveillance systems evaluated on crime rates

no_unlike_literature.description: The results of the paper show no significant effect of the video surveillance systems evaluated on crime rates, unlike what is reported in the literature

no_but_mixed_results.description: The results of the paper show no significant overall effect of the video surveillance systems evaluated on crime rates, but there are mixed results on specific cases

maybe.description: The results of the paper suggest that the video surveillance systems evaluated might have an effect on crime rates, but the evidence is not strong enough to conclude

yes_but_low_confidence.description: The results of the paper suggest that the video surveillance systems evaluated may reduce crime rates, but the evidence is not strong

yes_but_small_effect.description: The results of the paper suggest that the video surveillance systems evaluated may have a small effect on crime rates

yes.description: The results of the paper suggest that the video surveillance systems evaluated reduce crime rates

papers.title: Évaluation des effets de la télé-surveillance sur la criminalité commise dans 13 stations du métro de Montréal
papers.quote: Our analyses have been unable to detect any overall impact of CCTV cameras on the behavior of offenders. And controlling for kinds of crime or for specific areas and places within subway stations (depending on the location of cameras) did not change or qualify the initial overall no-effect finding

papers.title: Effects of Closed Circuit Television Surveillance on Crime
papers.quote: CCTV has a modest impact on crime. Effectiveness varies across settings. Surveillance is more effective at preventing crime in car parks, and less effective in city and town centers, public housing, and public transport

papers.title: La télésurveillance policière dans les lieux publics: l'apprentissage d'une technologie
papers.quote: CCTV did manage to have an impact on the incidence of drugdealing transactions as well as a collateral impact on the incidence of other offences, especially violent crimes. The second and more common approach (passive), however, had no impact on crime

papers.title: Evaluation of Camera Use to Prevent Crime in Commuter Parking Facilities: A Randomized Controlled Trial
papers.quote: Both theory and prior research support this study’s findings that the cameras had no discernable impact on crime. [...] cameras are most likely to have an impact when they are highly concentrated, actively monitored, and well integrated into law enforcement crime control and investigative activities

papers.title: Police-monitored CCTV cameras in Newark, NJ: A quasi-experimental test of crime deterrence
papers.quote: Overall, the system of cameras in Newark is not as efficient as it could be at deterring certain crimes. Some camera places are more effective than others. [...] The system of cameras in Newark significantly deters auto theft city-wide. However, shootings and thefts from autos are only deterred by cameras installed in certain places

papers.title: The crime-reduction effects of open-street CCTV in South Korea
papers.quote: On average, open-street CCTV did not show a statistically significant effect on the reduction of serious crimes or disorder crimes. [...] The crime-reduction effects of open-street CCTV were different in each open-street CCTV location

papers.title: Crime-Reduction Effects of Open-street CCTV: Conditionality Considerations
papers.quote: Overall, the findings provided minimal evidence of the effectiveness of CCTV in reducing crime, though some types of crime were reduced in residential areas especially, and effectiveness was clearly interdependent with an area’s base rate of crime. [...] CCTV had significant reduction effects on assault, robbery, and burglary in residential areas, but it did not have significant reduction effects on auto theft and theft from auto in any location type

papers.title: Hot Spot Policing With Actively Monitored CCTV Cameras
papers.quote: The results presented in this study suggest that the implementation of operational CCTV cameras at the square Stortorget in the town of Malmo¨ to improve directed patrol efforts has not had a significant crime-reducing effect on assaults

notes.title: Difference between American and Swedish context
notes.description:
"The main contribution of this article was to show that actively monitored CCTV cameras with directed patrols at hot spots of violent crime may be less effective in a Swedish context
than it appears to be in the North America."

papers.title: Exploring the effects of CCTV upon fear of crime: A multi-level approach in Seoul
papers.quote: The results showed that the number of CCTV cameras was negatively associated with the fear of crime, but no significant effect was observed on the perceived risk of crime. In addition, the effects of CCTV differed by gender

papers.title: Surveillance cameras and crime: a review of randomized and natural experiments
papers.quote: Included studies that reported changes in total crime found overall crime reductions ranging from 24–28% in public street settings and urban subway stations [...] but no desirable effects in commuter parking facilities or suburban subway stations

papers.title: The effect of public surveillance cameras on crime clearance rates
papers.quote: Several findings suggest some promising uses of a CCTV as an investigative tool which enhances crime clearance. Relative to what clearance rates were before cameras were installed, CCTV's appeared to increase clearances of crimes by around 2%. [...] However, this effect appears to be mostly limited to thefts, and decays by around 500 feet

papers.title: Estimating the impact of an integrated CCTV program on crime
papers.quote: Over time, property crimes and disorder crimes decreased faster relative to the matched controls. There was little evidence of any impact on violent crimes

papers.title: Urban Video Surveillance as a Tool to Improve Security in Public Spaces
papers.quote: The Katowice Municipal Police Headquarters recorded noticeable decreases in the number of preparatory proceedings in the seven categories of particularly onerous crimes (27% for all categories, including 24.9% for robberies, 20.2% for brawls and batteries, 16.1% for burglaries, 20.3% for theft of property, 16.4% for damage to property, and 31.4% for vehicle theft. Only in the damage to health category an increase of 16.4% was observed

notes.title: Study over two time periods
notes.description: The study compared the results of the camera installation in Katowice in 2001 and again in 2017. In 2001, there were no conclusive results, but the results were much more significant in 2017. This follows the national trend. Surveillance cameras also had a deterrent effect, although the reduction in crime may also be linked to other factors.

papers.title: THE DETERRENT EFFECT OF SURVEILLANCE CAMERAS ON CRIME
papers.quote: The results suggest that crime drops at grids under direct surveillance by 0.011 per month, on average. Given the large number of grids exposed to direct surveillance, these effects add up to a relatively large number of deterred crimes

papers.title: The internationalisation of cctv surveillance: Effects on crime and implications for emerging technologies
papers.quote: The cumulative evidence demonstrates that CCTV surveillance is associated with significant yet modest reductions in crime and the effects vary across a range of contextual factors, including country of origin

papers.title: Video Surveillance System Usage in Preventing Crime: Preliminary findings from Malaysia
papers.quote: The findings suggest that video surveillance systems can effectively deter and reduce criminal activities. However, several challenges still need to be addressed, including limited expertise in video analysis and the high costs associated with these systems

papers.title: Effects of CCTV on Fear of Crime: a Systematic Literature Review
papers.quote: The overall effects were inconclusive. Seven studies showed reductions in fear of crime; six showed mixed, marginal or no effects; and two showed increases
